newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Energy Secretary choices narrowing-sources.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Energy Secretary choices narrowing-sources.

text.p: Choices for the next U.S. Secretary of Energy appeared to be focused on Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Chairwoman Elizabeth Moler and University of California-Berkeley Chancellor Chang-Lin-Tien, a number of sources said Monday.
While other names still were being bandied about, those were the two that sources from industry and environmental groups as well as Capitol Hill said appeared most prominent.
Others also mentioned were Deputy Energy Secretary Charles Curtis, retiring Louisiana Democratic Senator Bennett Johnston, and Nuclear Regulatory Commission Chairwoman Shirley Jackson.

Midwestern agricultural interests pushed Nebraska Governor Benjamin Nelson, who founded the Governors' Ethanol Coalition and headed the 36-state Interstate Oil and Gas Compact Commission, but few sources expected him to have much chance.
Tien, pushed by a number of California's Democratic congressmen, has emerged as a front-runner along with Moler.

In a letter to President Clinton, 14 California congressmen said: "Chancellor Tien's distinguished career as an educator in the field of mechanical engineering... makes him particularly suited to lead the Department of Energy."
Moler, with a Washington track record on energy issues, appeared to have fairly solid industry support.
"Moler is very well liked on the Hill. She's no-nosense, no galavanting about, and she knows the issues," one industry source said.
